tags.author: FA Chancellor Roberts and Philipp Arndt
tags.description: Very fun movement on positive edges. Eases up towards the top. To keep the grade in the 5.10 range you will need to aid through the first bolt, which can be clipped from the ground. Stepping into some slings will do. 4 bolts to a gear anchor.
tags.name: Lethal Lemonade

tags.author: FA Philipp Arndt
tags.description: A short but sweet finger crack that goes surprisingly easy for how steeply overhung it is (~15 degrees). 2-bolt anchor with rap rings.
tags.name: Trunk Tribute

tags.author: FA Michael Sandler and Philipp Arndt
tags.description: Thin and friction-y moves on a fairly low-angle slab. The crux is getting your feet onto the slopy hold on top of the small overlap. 2-bolt anchor, walk-off on the south side.
tags.name: Dangermilk

tags.author: FA Michael Sandler and Philipp Arndt
tags.description: Traversing slab route with mostly positive holds and and interesting sequence. The crux comes after the second bolt, where the right-trending foot ledge tapers out. 2-bolt anchor. Walk-off on the south side.
tags.name: Forbidden Gatorade

tags.author: FA Rick Piggot
tags.description: Climb the obvious flake until it seams out, then switch to harder face climbing past bolts.
tags.name: PhD

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Overhanging jugs to layback on a seam. Reach move crux near the top. 2-bolt anchor for TR
tags.name: The Cave

tags.author: FA Dick Cilley
tags.description: Steep lieback to a throw for the top.
tags.name: Alcoa

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Thin face up the center of the boulder.
tags.name: Stairway to Heaven

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Three routes (left: 5.11+, center: 5.11, right: 5.11-) all slabby face climbs on perfect rock, requiring delicate footwork. Toprope only.
tags.name: Starface

tags.author: FA Philipp Arndt, 2023
tags.description: Wide stemming chimney, 2-bolt anchor and 3 bolts for the lead.
tags.name: The Learning Cave Chimney

tags.author: Philipp Arndt, Jan 2024
tags.description: C4 cams size #0.5 to #3, with doubles #1-#2. Extra #2s probably won't go unused. Two-bolt anchor.Probably the longest continuous crack on the main hill. Nice-looking jams are so deep in the flare that it feels more like an offwidth. TR with directionals.
tags.name: Five-Nine Handcrack

tags.author: Royal Robbins, 1969
tags.description: Most classic splitter crack at Woodson
tags.name: Robbins Crack

tags.description: Start by swinging to the obvious jug (or jumping if you are short), then make your way up the crack.
tags.name: Kaleidoskopik Karussell

tags.description: 60 ft of finger crack liebacking to easier slab near the top. The crux is the first 15ft where the crack is thin and the wall is steep. Small cams (0.1-0.5) and a #2 for the top. 2 bolt anchor
tags.name: Victory at Sea

tags.author: Peter Gompper
tags.description: Splitter tips crack with delicate feet. A Woodson classic, and long for the area. Small to medium cams and nuts, 2-bolt anchor.
tags.name: Cat Crack

tags.author: Philipp Arndt and Alexia Fabiani, May 2024
tags.description: Slabby route with a striking white dike running directly up the middle of the face. Interesting moves on mostly flakey crimps. 4 bolts and 2-bolt anchor.
tags.name: Plutonacious

tags.note: Small rope to climb over short, approximately 2.5 meter cliff

tags.author: project
tags.description: No known ascents as of Dec 2025. Long, right-leaning, overhung crack. Offwidth to flared tips (crux) to mostly fingers. Seems to stay wet for multiple days after it rains.
tags.name: Hard And Soul (project)

tags.description: Surprisingly fun and geometric climbing leads to a distinct offwidth crux. Watch out for poison oak, it might sprout out of the crack again.
tags.name: Battle of Urushiol

tags.description: Low-angle less than vertical crack in a dihedral. Starts with hands and widens all the way to offwidth near the top. Watch out for poison oak.
tags.name: Pac-Man

tags.description: Hands to offwidth, slightly overhung. Woodson classic.
tags.name: Crucible

tags.author: unknown
tags.description: Somewhat awkward start to an awesome splitter hand crack. Woodson classic.
tags.name: Out Of Sight

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: The name says it all. A few grunty offwidth moves to an awesome chimney solo. No bolts, but the solo is secure. A Woodson classic.
tags.name: Big Grunt

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Perfect dihedral with a splitter wide hands crack to a mantle at the top. A Woodson classic.
tags.name: Rockwork Orange

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Good hand crack on a dihedral leads to off width as you climb higher. Bolted anchor.
tags.name: Fake Phantom Crack

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Splitter fingers to ringlocks crack. A short Woodson classic.
tags.name: Jaws

tags.author: FA Greg Cameron
tags.description: Two cruxes, one knee/calf lock offwidth at the bottom, and another bouldery one at the top. A Woodson classic.
tags.name: Mother Superior

tags.description: Thin splitter crack up a less than vertical face, widening towards the top. Thin tips at the start are the crux. A Woodson classic.
tags.name: Hard as Nails

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Splitter tight hand crack on less than vertical rock. Everyone's first trad lead at Woodson. Gear anchor -- keep your rope out of the crack!
tags.name: Elsa's Crack

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Roadside moderate flared fist crack / offwidth. 2-bolt anchor. Need to lead first to set a toprope.
tags.name: Poison Oak Crack

tags.author: Yoav Altman (TR), Erik Roed (lead)
tags.description: Splitter crack -- mostly sweet finger locks, with the crux near the top, as the crack widens slightly and steepens to just past vertical. Gear anchor.
tags.name: Yoav Crack

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Nice moderate hands to offwidth crack (BD C4 #2-#6). Great for learning some OW technique.
tags.name: Sickle Crack

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Woodson's most classic pure boulder problem. In the little shaded cave-like area on the inside of the switchback. Hand traverse from the left to right, to a big exit move out right. Hard.
tags.name: The Fake Eppulator

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Great thin finger crack. 2-bolt anchor for TR and lowering.
tags.name: Digit's Delight

tags.author: FA unknown
tags.description: Fun finger crack in a low-angle corner. Gear anchor.
tags.name: Milkbar

tags.description: A very popular climbing route and the easiest up Liberty Bell. Approach via the gully nearly to its highest point, then follow a small rock ledge back to a larger ledge where multiple first pitch variations can be taken. A short scramble to the summit mus
tags.name: Beckey Route

tags.description: The easiest route up Lexington Tower. Start at the highest point of the notch between Concord and Lexington Towers (approach via the west gully, or by rappelling the South Face of Concord Tower). The second pitch ends at the notch between Lexington Tower'
tags.name: Lexington Tower North Face

tags.description: The easiest climbing route up Concord Tower. Start at the very top of the notch between Liberty and Concord, approached the same way as for Beckey Route. Descend from rappel anchors at summit (back down the route, or on the South face to access Lexington)

tags.description: Climb a bulge to easier terrain, then up the steeper face to an overlap (crux). Surmount the overlap and continue up the slab toward the anchor with another steep section toward the top.

I Can't Believe It's Not Butte-r

tags.description: Begins about 2/3 of the way down the descent path from Great Red Book. Climb short left-leaning crack to a bolted anchor with rappel rings. Look for 3 protection bolts near start of route (the crux).
tags.name: Cromulent Crack
